card.name: Linking words before lab animal species
card.fires_on: Small linking words like in, of, to, and or and right after a carcinogenicity or toxicity study is mentioned, just before the animal species (mice, rats) is named.

modes.label: Study in animals
modes.description: The word 'in' after 'study' or 'studies', right before rats or mice.
modes.example: In a 2-year study<< in>> rats at three oral dosage levels of up

modes.label: Joining species or sexes
modes.description: 'and' or 'male' used in a list of animal groups or strains.
modes.example: Lifetime carcinogenicity studies were carried out in CD-1 mice<< and>> Long-Evans rats at doses up

modes.label: Dosing verb link
modes.description: 'to' or 'of' after administered or mating pairs, before a rodent strain.
modes.example: In 13 week toxicity studies, theophylline was administered<< to>> F344 rats and B6

card.writes: It seems to push toward rodent strain names and breeding or lab-animal wording.
card.plain: It marks the spot in animal toxicology text where the type of lab animal is about to be named.
